mcqs.question: The first Supreme Court in British India was established under which Act?
mcqs.explanation: The Regulating Act, 1773 established the first Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta, in 1774.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Charter Act, 1813 provided for spending at least ₹1 lakh per year on the education of Indians.
The Charter Act, 1813 introduced open competition for Civil Services.
The first provision for spending on education of Indians was made by the Charter Act, 1813.
The Charter Act, 1813 ended the Company’s trade monopoly in India except in tea and China trade.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the introduction of open competition for Civil Services. That was introduced by the Charter Act, 1853.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Charter Act, 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
Reason (R): Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the fact that Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India does not explain the legislative change made by the Act.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Charter Act, 1853
(b) Government of India Act, 1858
(c) Indian Councils Act, 1909
(d) Government of India Act, 1919

List-II
(i) Direct elections
(ii) Lord Canning became first Viceroy
(iii) Open competition for Civil Services
(iv) Separate electorate for Muslims
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Charter Act 1853–open competition, 1858 Act–Canning, 1909 Act–separate electorate, and 1919 Act–direct elections.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the Constitution
B. First meeting of the Constituent Assembly
C. Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru
D. Objectives Resolution adopted
mcqs.explanation: The sequence was first meeting on 9 December 1946, Objectives Resolution moved on 13 December 1946, its adoption on 22 January 1947, and adoption of the Constitution on 26 November 1949.

mcqs.question: Who was the first permanent elected Chairman/President of the Constituent Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first permanent elected Chairman/President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the First Amendment Act, 1951:
I. It added the Ninth Schedule.
II. It added clause (4) to Article 15.
III. It added Articles 31A and 31B.
IV. It introduced the parliamentary form of government.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct features mentioned in the notes. The parliamentary form of government was first introduced in Great Britain, not by the First Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The parliamentary form of government was first introduced in Great Britain.
Statement B: The presidential form was first formed in the USA.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are directly supported by the notes.

mcqs.question: Who was the first President of India?
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The first joint sitting of Parliament was held in 1961.
Reason (R): It was held for the Dowry Prohibition Bill.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Dowry Prohibition Bill explains the occasion of the first joint sitting in 1961.

mcqs.question:
Match the parliamentary committees with the year or description associated with them.
List-I
(a) Public Accounts Committee
(b) Estimates Committee
(c) Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee
(d) Lok Sabha Ethics Committee

List-II
(i) First constituted in 1950
(ii) First set up in 1921
(iii) First such committee by any Indian legislature, constituted in 1997
(iv) First constituted in 2000
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are PAC–1921, Estimates Committee–1950, Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee–1997, and Lok Sabha Ethics Committee–2000.

mcqs.question: Who was the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court of India?
mcqs.explanation: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court in 1989.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The doctrine of Judicial Review was first propounded in the USA.
Reason (R): It was first propounded in the case of Marbury v. Madison in 1803.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Marbury v. Madison decision explains the association of the doctrine with the USA.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Basic Structure doctrine was first propounded in Kesavananda Bharati in 1973.
II. Fundamental Rights were first held amendable in the Shankari Prasad case.
III. The first PIL considered was Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar.
IV. The Federal Court was inaugurated in 1950.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The Federal Court was inaugurated on 1 October 1937, not in 1950.

mcqs.question: Who was the first woman Governor of any State in India?
mcqs.explanation: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of any State, serving in Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.question:
Match the institutions or commissions with the persons associated with their first leadership.
List-I
(a) National Human Rights Commission
(b) Law Commission of Independent India
(c) Election Commission
(d) Planning Commission Deputy Chairmanship

List-II
(i) Sukumar Sen
(ii) Justice Ranganath Misra
(iii) M.C. Setalvad
(iv) Gulzarilal Nanda
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are NHRC–Justice Ranganath Misra, Law Commission–M.C. Setalvad, Election Commission–Sukumar Sen, and Planning Commission Deputy Chairman–Gulzarilal Nanda.

mcqs.question: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
mcqs.explanation: Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner, serving from 1950 to 1958.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Political parties received constitutional recognition for the first time in 1985.
2. Tamil was declared the first Classical Language.
3. Madras was the first Municipal Corporation in India.
4. Andhra Pradesh was the first state to inaugurate Panchayati Raj.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Rajasthan was the first state to inaugurate Panchayati Raj, while Andhra Pradesh was the second.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Community Development Programme
B. National Extension Service
C. Panchayati Raj inaugurated at Nagaur
D. Constitutional recognition of political parties
mcqs.explanation: The sequence is Community Development Programme in 1952, National Extension Service in 1953, Panchayati Raj at Nagaur in 1959, and constitutional recognition of political parties in 1985.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated on 2 October 1959 in Nagaur, Rajasthan.
Statement B: Rajasthan was the first state and Andhra Pradesh was the second state to inaugurate Panchayati Raj.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta
(b) First Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William
(c) First Law Member of the Governor-General’s Council
(d) Section 87 of the Charter Act, 1833

List-II
(i) Macaulay
(ii) 1774
(iii) Opened Company service to Indians without discrimination based on religion or colour
(iv) Sir Elijah Impey

Which of the following is the correct code?
mcqs.explanation: The first Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta, was established in 1774, with Sir Elijah Impey as its first Chief Justice. Macaulay was the first Law Member of the Governor-General’s Council, while Section 87 opened Company service to Indians without discrimination based on religion or colour.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Charter Act 1853 separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General’s Council for the first time.
Reason (R): The Charter Act 1853 introduced open competition for Civil Services.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Act first separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General’s Council and also introduced open competition for Civil Services, but the latter did not explain the former.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act, 1909:

I. It associated Indians with the Viceroy’s Executive Council for the first time.
II. It associated Indians with the Governors’ Executive Councils for the first time.
III. Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian Law Member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Indian Councils Act 1909 marked the first association of Indians with both the Viceroy’s and Governors’ Executive Councils, and Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian Law Member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Indian Councils Act, 1909
(b) Lord Minto
(c) Government of India Act, 1919
(d) Separate electorate for Muslims

List-II
(i) Feature introduced by the Indian Councils Act, 1909
(ii) Father of Communal Electorate
(iii) Morley-Minto reforms
(iv) Montagu-Chelmsford reforms

Which of the following is the correct code?
mcqs.explanation: The Indian Councils Act 1909 was known as the Morley-Minto reforms and introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Lord Minto was called the Father of Communal Electorate, while the Government of India Act 1919 was known as the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1919:

I. It made the Central Legislature bicameral for the first time.
II. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces for the first time.
III. It used the term “responsible government” for the first time.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 first made the Central Legislature bicameral, introduced dyarchy in the provinces, and used the term “responsible government.”

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:

I. It provided for an All-India Federation for the first time.
II. The All-India Federation provided for by the Act never came into existence.
III. It introduced dyarchy at the Centre.
IV. Dyarchy at the Centre was never implemented.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The Act first provided for an All-India Federation, but it never came into existence; it also introduced dyarchy at the Centre, which was never implemented.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces
(b) Establishment of the Federal Court
(c) First Chief Justice of the Federal Court
(d) Separation of Burma from India

List-II
(i) Federal Court
(ii) Government of India Act, 1935
(iii) Burma was separated from India
(iv) Sir Maurice Gwyer

Which of the following is the correct code?
mcqs.explanation: The Government of India Act 1935 abolished dyarchy in the provinces and separated Burma from India. It established the Federal Court, whose first Chief Justice was Sir Maurice Gwyer.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Government of India Act, 1935 created Sindh as a new province.
Statement B: The Government of India Act, 1935 created Orissa as a new province.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Government of India Act 1935 created Sindh and Orissa as new provinces.

mcqs.question: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, in whom were the residuary powers vested?
mcqs.explanation: The Government of India Act 1935 vested residuary powers in the Governor-General.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) M.N. Roy
(b) Swaraj Party
(c) Constituent Assembly
(d) Ranchi conference

List-II
(i) Idea of a Constituent Assembly first put forward in 1934
(ii) First formal demand for a Constituent Assembly
(iii) Held in May 1934
(iv) Constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946
mcqs.explanation: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea in 1934. The Swaraj Party made the first formal demand at its Ranchi conference in May 1934, while the Constituent Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:

I. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President of its first meeting.
II. Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the permanent elected Chairman or President on 11 December 1946.
III. Frank Anthony was the first nominated temporary Deputy Chairman.
IV. H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Sinha presided temporarily at the first meeting; Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946; Frank Anthony was the first nominated temporary Deputy Chairman; and H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Objectives Resolution was moved at the fifth meeting of the first session of the Constituent Assembly.
Statement B: H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Objectives Resolution was moved at the fifth meeting of the first session, and H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Constitution of India fully came into force on 26 January 1950.
Reason (R): B.N. Rau prepared the first draft of the Constitution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the preparation of the first draft by B.N. Rau does not explain why the Constitution came fully into force on 26 January 1950.

mcqs.question: How many women members were there in the Constituent Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: The Constituent Assembly had 15 women members.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Interim Government of 1946:

I. It was announced on 24 August 1946.
II. It took charge on 2 September 1946.
III. Jawaharlal Nehru was the Vice-President of the Executive Council.
IV. R.K. Shanmukham Chetty was the first Finance Minister of independent India.
V. Some sources also mention John Mathai as a later Finance Minister of independent India.
options: I, III, IV and V only
I, II, IV and V only
I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. The Interim Government was announced on 24 August, took charge on 2 September, had Nehru as Vice-President of the Executive Council, and R.K. Shanmukham Chetty as the first Finance Minister; John Mathai is also mentioned as a later Finance Minister by some sources.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Constitution of India Bill of 1895 made the first explicit demand for Fundamental Rights.
Statement B: The First Amendment Act, 1951 restricted the rights under Article 19, while the First Schedule lists the States and Union Territories.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Constitution of India Bill of 1895 made the first explicit demand for Fundamental Rights; the First Amendment restricted Article 19 rights, and the First Schedule lists the States and Union Territories.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(b) Pratibha Patil
(c) Droupadi Murmu
(d) Dr. S. Radhakrishnan

List-II
(i) First Vice-President of India
(ii) First woman President of India
(iii) First President of India; from Bihar
(iv) First tribal woman President of India
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Dr. Rajendra Prasad—first President of India and from Bihar; Pratibha Patil—first woman President; Droupadi Murmu—first tribal woman President; and Dr. S. Radhakrishnan—first Vice-President.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
(b) Indira Gandhi
(c) Acharya J.B. Kripalani
(d) First no-confidence motion

List-II
(i) First Deputy Prime Minister of India
(ii) First Prime Minister who was a Rajya Sabha member at the time of appointment
(iii) Moved against Nehru’s government
(iv) Moved in the Third Lok Sabha in 1963
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the first Deputy Prime Minister, while Indira Gandhi was the first Prime Minister who was a Rajya Sabha member at appointment. Kripalani moved the first no-confidence motion against Nehru’s government, and it was moved in the Third Lok Sabha in 1963.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The first general election to the Lok Sabha was held in 1951–52.
II. The first session of the First Lok Sabha began on 13 May 1952.
III. The first session of the First Lok Sabha began on 9 December 1946.
mcqs.explanation: The first Lok Sabha general election was held in 1951–52, and the first session of the First Lok Sabha began on 13 May 1952. The date 9 December 1946 relates to the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly, not the First Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Nargis Dutt
(b) Nargis Dutt’s nomination to the Rajya Sabha
(c) Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha

List-II
(i) First actress nominated to the Rajya Sabha
(ii) 1980
(iii) First recognised in 1969
mcqs.explanation: Nargis Dutt was the first actress nominated to the Rajya Sabha, and her nomination took place in 1980. The Leader of the Opposition was first recognised in the Lok Sabha in 1969.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chamber of Princes
(b) Creation of the Chamber of Princes
(c) Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner

List-II
(i) 120 members
(ii) Government of India Act 1919
(iii) First Chancellor of the Chamber of Princes
mcqs.explanation: The Chamber of Princes had 120 members and was created under the Government of India Act 1919. Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner was its first Chancellor.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Public Accounts Committee
(b) Federal Court
(c) Sir Maurice Gwyer

List-II
(i) Set up first in 1921 under the Government of India Act 1919
(ii) Established under the Government of India Act 1935
(iii) First Chief Justice of the Federal Court
mcqs.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act 1919. The Federal Court was established under the Government of India Act 1935, and Sir Maurice Gwyer was its first Chief Justice.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court in 1989.
Statement B: Justice M. Fathima Beevi was the first Muslim woman in the higher judiciary.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court in 1989 and was also the first Muslim woman in the higher judiciary.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Sarojini Naidu
(b) Sarojini Naidu’s State
(c) Sucheta Kripalani
(d) Sucheta Kripalani’s State

List-II
(i) First woman Governor of any State
(ii) Uttar Pradesh
(iii) First woman Chief Minister of any State
(iv) Uttar Pradesh
mcqs.explanation: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of any State, serving in Uttar Pradesh. Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister of any State and was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The first imposition of President’s Rule is associated with both PEPSU in 1953 and Punjab in 1951 in different accounts.
Reason (R): Sources vary slightly regarding whether PEPSU in 1953 or Punjab in 1951 was the first instance of President’s Rule under Article 356.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason explains the apparent difference: one account identifies PEPSU in 1953, while sources that vary slightly identify Punjab in 1951 as the first imposition under Article 356.

mcqs.question: According to one account, in which year was the First Finance Commission constituted?
mcqs.explanation: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 according to one account. The notes also mention that it was set up in 1952 under K.C. Neogy, reflecting a variation in accounts.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Finance Commission—year of setup according to another account
(b) First Chairman of the Finance Commission
(c) First Chairman of the Planning Commission
(d) First Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog

List-II
(i) 1952
(ii) K.C. Neogy
(iii) Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru
(iv) Arvind Panagariya
mcqs.explanation: According to another account, the First Finance Commission was set up in 1952, with K.C. Neogy as its first Chairman. Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Chairman of the Planning Commission, while Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog.

mcqs.question: Who was the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission?
mcqs.explanation: Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru was the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: According to one account, the Inter-State Council was first established in May 1990.
Statement B: According to another account, the Inter-State Council was first established in December 1990.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The sheet records two accounts: one places the first establishment of the Inter-State Council in May 1990, while another places it in December 1990.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809.
II. The First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in 1966.
III. The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas.
IV. Morarji Desai submitted the interim report of the First Administrative Reforms Commission.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Ombudsman originated in Sweden in 1809; the First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in 1966, recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas, and had its interim report submitted by Morarji Desai.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968.
Reason (R): Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was the first Lokpal of India.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the identity of the first Lokpal does not explain the year in which the first Lokpal Bill was presented.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Maharashtra as the first state to introduce Lokayukta
(b) Year of introduction of Lokayukta in Maharashtra
(c) Odisha as the first state to pass a Lokayukta Act

List-II
(i) 1971 or 1972
(ii) First state to pass a Lokayukta Act
(iii) First state to introduce Lokayukta
(iv) 1968
mcqs.explanation: Maharashtra was the first state to introduce the Lokayukta, in 1971 or 1972. Odisha was the first state to pass a Lokayukta Act.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission—year of assumption of office
(b) First Law Commission of independent India—year of establishment
(c) Public Service Commission—legal basis of first establishment
(d) Public Service Commission—date of establishment

List-II
(i) 1993
(ii) 1955
(iii) Government of India Act 1919
(iv) 1 October 1926
mcqs.explanation: The first Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission assumed office in 1993. The First Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955, while the Public Service Commission was first established under the Government of India Act 1919 on 1 October 1926.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chief Election Commissioner during 1950–1958
(b) First woman Chief Election Commissioner
(c) Amendment that lowered the voting age to 18
(d) First exercise of voting age of 18

List-II
(i) Sukumar Sen
(ii) V.S. Ramadevi
(iii) 61st Amendment
(iv) 1989 General Election
mcqs.explanation: Sukumar Sen served as Chief Election Commissioner from 1950 to 1958, and V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner. The voting age was lowered to 18 by the 61st Amendment and was first exercised in the 1989 General Election.

mcqs.question: VVPAT was first used in which of the following elections?
options: First General Election to the Lok Sabha
mcqs.explanation: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland on 4 September 2013.

mcqs.question: VVPAT was first used in which of the following?
options: Noksen Assembly by-election, Nagaland, on 4 September 2013
First General Election to the Lok Sabha, 1951–52
mcqs.explanation: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland on 4 September 2013.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Constitutional recognition to political parties
(b) First President of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh
(c) First President of the BJP
(d) Year Atal Bihari Vajpayee became the first President of the BJP

List-II
(i) 52nd Amendment and Tenth Schedule
(ii) Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee
(iii) Atal Bihari Vajpayee
(iv) 1980
mcqs.explanation: The 52nd Amendment provided constitutional recognition to political parties through the Tenth Schedule or anti-defection provisions. Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee was the first President of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, while Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the first President of the BJP in 1980.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The First Official Language Commission was established in 1955.
Statement B: B.G. Kher headed the First Official Language Commission.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct: the First Official Language Commission was established in 1955 and was headed by B.G. Kher.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The first Municipal Corporation in India was established at Madras in 1688.
II. Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur by Jawaharlal Nehru.
III. Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the 73rd Amendment in its true spirit.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Madras had the first Municipal Corporation in India in 1688; Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur; and Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the 73rd Amendment in its true spirit.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was the first major rural development programme after independence?
mcqs.explanation: The Community Development Programme was the first major rural development programme after independence.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Speaker of the Lok Sabha
(b) First Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925
(c) First permanent elected Chairman/President of the Constituent Assembly
(d) Temporary President at the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly

List-II
(i) G.V. Mavalankar
(ii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(iii) Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
(iv) Frank Anthony
mcqs.explanation: G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha and had also been the first Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first permanent elected Chairman/President of the Constituent Assembly, while Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was its temporary President at the first meeting.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I

mcqs.explanation: The parliamentary form of government was borrowed from Britain, DPSP from Ireland, federation with a strong Centre from Canada, and the Concurrent List from Australia.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The procedure established by law was borrowed from Japan.
The idea of a Republic was borrowed from France.
The procedure for constitutional amendment was borrowed from Ireland.
Emergency provisions, except financial emergency, were borrowed from Germany.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the source of the constitutional amendment procedure. It was borrowed from South Africa, not Ireland.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the USSR (Russia).
Reason (R): The ideals of Justice—social, economic and political—in the Preamble were also borrowed from the USSR (Russia).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. However, the USSR's contribution of the ideals of Justice is a separate borrowed feature and does not explain why Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the USSR.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Judicial Review was borrowed from the USA.
II. The post of Vice-President was borrowed from the USA.
III. Removal of Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts was borrowed from the USA.
IV. The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from France.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from the USA, not France, so statement IV is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided the structural and administrative backbone for the Constitution.
Statement B: The language of the Preamble was borrowed from Australia.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are supported by the notes. The Government of India Act, 1935 supplied the structural and administrative backbone, while the language of the Preamble was borrowed from Australia.

mcqs.question: The Cabinet system in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from which country?
mcqs.explanation: The Cabinet system was borrowed from Britain (UK).

mcqs.question: Who first conceived the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934?
mcqs.explanation: The first idea of a Constituent Assembly was given by M.N. Roy in 1934.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the composition and election of the Constituent Assembly is incorrect?
options: The total seats planned were 389, comprising 296 from British India and 93 from the Princely States.
British India had 292 seats from Governor’s provinces and 4 from Chief Commissioners’ provinces.
The elections to the Constituent Assembly were held in June–July 1946.
The representation ratio was one member per 10 lakh population.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the election period. Elections were held in July–August 1946, not June–July 1946.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Constituent Assembly was elected indirectly.
Reason (R): Its members were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Assembly members were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies, making the election indirect.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Union Constitution Committee
(b) Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities & Tribal Areas
(c) Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee
(d) Steering Committee

List-II
(i) Sardar Patel
(ii) Jawaharlal Nehru
(iii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(iv) J.B. Kripalani
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Union Constitution Committee—Jawaharlal Nehru; Advisory Committee—Sardar Patel; Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee—J.B. Kripalani; Steering Committee—Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Constituent Assembly:

I. The total seats planned were 389.
II. British India and the Princely States were allocated 296 and 93 seats respectively.
III. The representation ratio was one member per 10 lakh population.
IV. There were 15 women members.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct according to the notes on the composition of the Constituent Assembly.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

A. Objectives Resolution adopted
B. Drafting Committee formed
C. Constitution adopted
D. Objectives Resolution moved
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence is: Objectives Resolution moved on 13 December 1946, adopted on 22 January 1947, Drafting Committee formed on 29 August 1947, and Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following committees were chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad?

1. Steering Committee
2. Rules of Procedure Committee
3. Flag Committee (Ad-hoc)
4. Union Powers Committee
mcqs.explanation: Three committees—the Steering Committee, Rules of Procedure Committee and Flag Committee (Ad-hoc)—were chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The Union Powers Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly.
Statement B: B.N. Rau prepared the first draft containing 243 Articles and 13 Schedules.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor and prepared the first draft with 243 Articles and 13 Schedules.

mcqs.question: How many Schedules are present in the Constitution at present?
mcqs.explanation: The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules and presently has 12 Schedules. Four new Schedules were added later through Constitutional Amendments.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment in 1951.
The 11th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment in 1992.
The 12th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment in 1992.
The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the amendment associated with the 11th Schedule. It was added by the 73rd Amendment in 1992; the 12th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The 9th Schedule was added to protect land reform laws from judicial review.
Reason (R): The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment in 1951, and it validates certain Acts and Regulations, mainly land reforms.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 9th Schedule was introduced by the 1st Amendment in 1951 to validate certain Acts and Regulations, mainly land reform laws, and protect them from judicial review.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First Schedule
(b) Fourth Schedule
(c) Seventh Schedule
(d) Tenth Schedule

List-II
(i) Anti-Defection Law
(ii) Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to States and Union Territories
(iii) Names of States and Union Territories and their territorial extent
(iv) Division of powers among Union, State and Concurrent Lists
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: First Schedule—names and territorial extent of States and Union Territories; Fourth Schedule—Rajya Sabha seat allocation; Seventh Schedule—division of powers; Tenth Schedule—Anti-Defection Law.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Eighth Schedule originally contained 14 languages and presently contains 22 languages.
II. Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Amendment in 1967.
III. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.
IV. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment in 1992, not by the 92nd Amendment.

6.title: Parts and Articles of the Constitution

mcqs.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with Tribunals?
mcqs.explanation: Part XIV-A deals with Tribunals and covers Articles 323-A to 323-B.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Part XVIII deals with Emergency Provisions and covers Articles 352 to 360.
Part XX deals with Amendment of the Constitution and contains Article 368.
Part XXI deals with Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions and covers Articles 369 to 395.
Part XIX deals with Miscellaneous provisions and covers Articles 361 to 367.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement alters the ending article of Part XXI. Part XXI covers Articles 369 to 392, while Part XXII covers Articles 393 to 395.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Part IX of the Constitution deals with the Panchayats.
Reason (R): Part IX was added by the 73rd Amendment in 1992.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Part IX deals with the Panchayats, and its inclusion is noted as having been made through the 73rd Amendment, 1992.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Part I
(b) Part II
(c) Part V
(d) Part XX

List-II
(i) Citizenship
(ii) The Union
(iii) Amendment of the Constitution
(iv) The Union and its Territory
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Part I–The Union and its Territory, Part II–Citizenship, Part V–The Union, and Part XX–Amendment of the Constitution.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Part III deals with Fundamental Rights and covers Articles 12 to 35.
II. Part XII deals with Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits and covers Articles 264 to 300-A.
III. Part XVII deals with Official Language and covers Articles 343 to 351.
IV. Part XX contains Article 368 relating to Amendment of the Constitution.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct according to the notes: Parts III, XII, XVII and XX cover the subjects and article ranges stated.

7.title: Prime Minister: Powers and Constitutional Position

mcqs.question: Article 74 of the Constitution provides for:
options: The 15% limit on the size of the Council of Ministers
The duties of the Prime Minister
The Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
The appointment and tenure of Ministers
mcqs.explanation: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Prime Minister is the real Executive Head of the Union.
The Prime Minister can be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister is responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the Prime Minister is responsible to the Rajya Sabha. The Prime Minister is responsible only to the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Prime Minister is the real Executive Head of the Union.
Reason (R): The President is the nominal or constitutional head.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President is the nominal or constitutional head, while the Prime Minister functions as the real Executive Head of the Union.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The oath of the Prime Minister is administered by the President.
Statement B: The resignation of the Prime Minister is addressed to the President.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: the President administers the Prime Minister’s oath, and the Prime Minister addresses resignation to the President.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following bodies are chaired by the Prime Minister?
I. NITI Aayog
II. National Development Council
III. National Integration Council
IV. Inter-State Council
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Chairman of NITI Aayog, the National Development Council, the National Integration Council and the Inter-State Council.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Article 74
 b. Article 75
 c. Article 78
 d. Article 75(3)

List-II
 i. Appointment, tenure and responsibility of Ministers
 ii. Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
 iii. Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
 iv. Duties of the Prime Minister
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iv and d-iii. Article 74 concerns aid and advice, Article 75 concerns Ministers, Article 78 concerns the Prime Minister’s duties, and Article 75(3) concerns collective responsibility.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements regarding the size of the Council of Ministers are correct?
1. The total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
2. The same 15% limit applies to the States, including the Chief Minister.
3. The 15% limit was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
4. Article 75(1A) contains the 15% limit.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The 15% limit, applicable to the Union and the States, was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, and is referred to in Article 75(1A).

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): If a No-Confidence Motion is passed, the entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, must resign.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha means that the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, must resign when a No-Confidence Motion is passed.

mcqs.question: Article 52 of the Constitution provides for:
options: The executive power of the Union
The term of office of the President
mcqs.explanation: Article 52 provides that there shall be a President of India. Article 53 deals with the executive power of the Union.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the election of the President is incorrect?
options: Disputes regarding the presidential election are decided finally by the Supreme Court.
Nominated members of Parliament participate in the election of the President.
The President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College.
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are part of the Electoral College.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that nominated members of Parliament participate. Nominated members of Parliament and State Legislative Councils do not participate in the presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President is the nominal or constitutional head of the State.
Reason (R): The real executive is the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President is the constitutional head, while the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister constitutes the real executive.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 52
(b) Article 53
(c) Article 72
(d) Article 123

List-II
(i) Executive power of the Union vested in the President
(ii) There shall be a President of India
(iii) Power to grant pardons and related relief
(iv) Ordinance-making power
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iii and d-iv. These correspond respectively to Articles 52, 53, 72 and 123.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the presidential election:
I. It is an indirect election.
II. It uses proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote and secret ballot.
III. Nominated members of Parliament participate in it.
IV. Disputes regarding the election are decided by the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct. Nominated members of Parliament do not participate in the presidential election, making Statement III incorrect.

mcqs.question: The resignation of the President is addressed to the:
mcqs.explanation: The President addresses the resignation to the Vice-President.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding vacancy in the office of the President is incorrect?
options: In case of death, resignation, removal or otherwise, the Vice-President acts as President.
If both the offices of President and Vice-President are vacant, the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court acts as President.
If both offices are vacant, the Prime Minister acts as President.
The Vice-President acts as President under Article 65 in the specified circumstances.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that the Prime Minister acts as President. If both offices are vacant, the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court acts as President.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies participate in the election of the President.
Reason (R): Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the impeachment of the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the non-participation of elected State Assembly members in impeachment does not explain their participation in the presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President can seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court, but that opinion is not binding.
Statement B: The President can return a Bill only once, except a Money Bill.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. The President may seek a non-binding advisory opinion under Article 143 and may return a Bill only once, except a Money Bill.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(b) Pratibha Patil
(c) Droupadi Murmu
(d) Chief Justice of India

List-II
(i) First Woman President
(ii) First President
(iii) Oath administrator to the President
(iv) First Tribal President
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Dr. Rajendra Prasad—First President, Pratibha Patil—First Woman President, Droupadi Murmu—First Tribal President, and Chief Justice of India—oath administrator.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following Articles relate to the emergency powers of the President?
1. Article 352
2. Article 356
3. Article 360
4. Article 143
mcqs.explanation: Three Articles—352, 356 and 360—relate to National Emergency, President’s Rule and Financial Emergency respectively. Article 143 concerns the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court.

mcqs.question: The President promulgates Ordinances when:
options: The Supreme Court is not in session
The Council of Ministers is not in office
The Lok Sabha has been dissolved permanently
mcqs.explanation: The President promulgates Ordinances when Parliament is not in session. The ordinance-making power is co-extensive with the legislative power of Parliament.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements correctly describe the President of India?
1. The executive power of the Union is exercised by the President directly or through officers subordinate to the President.
2. The President is the First Citizen of India.
3. The President is a symbol of the unity of the nation.
4. The President is a symbol of the integrity of the nation.
5. The President is a symbol of the solidarity of the nation.
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. The President exercises the Union’s executive power directly or through subordinate officers and is described as the First Citizen and a symbol of the nation’s unity, integrity and solidarity.

mcqs.question: Under Article 53(2), the President of India is the:
options: Final authority in disputes regarding presidential election
Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces
Chief executive of the Council of Ministers
mcqs.explanation: Article 53(2) identifies the President as the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Elected members of the Lok Sabha
(b) Elected members of the Rajya Sabha
(c) Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States
(d) Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

List-II
(i) Included in the Presidential Electoral College
(ii) Included in the Presidential Electoral College
(iii) Included in the Presidential Electoral College
(iv) Added to the Presidential Electoral College by the 70th Amendment
mcqs.explanation: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies form part of the Electoral College. Delhi and Puducherry were included by the 70th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The value of an MLA’s vote is calculated to ensure uniformity among the States.
Reason (R): The value of an MP’s vote is calculated to ensure parity between the Union and the States.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but they describe two distinct principles: uniformity among the States for MLA votes and parity between the Union and the States for MP votes.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Citizenship requirement
(b) Minimum age requirement
(c) Legislative qualification
(d) Office-related restriction

List-II
(i) Must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
(ii) Must not hold any office of profit
(iii) Must be a citizen of India
(iv) Must have completed 35 years of age
mcqs.explanation: A presidential candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, qualified for election to the Lok Sabha and must not hold an office of profit.

mcqs.question: Under Article 57, the President of India is:
options: Eligible for re-election any number of times
Eligible for re-election for two terms only
mcqs.explanation: Article 57 permits the President to be re-elected any number of times.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the impeachment of the President:
I. The President can be removed by impeachment for violation of the Constitution.
II. Article 61 deals with the impeachment of the President.
III. Either House of Parliament can prefer a charge for impeachment.
IV. A special majority is required in both Houses of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Impeachment for violation of the Constitution is dealt with under Article 61; either House may prefer the charge, and a special majority is required in both Houses.

mcqs.question: Which enactment deals with succession when both the offices of President and Vice-President are vacant?
options: The Representation of the People Act
mcqs.explanation: The President’s Succession Act deals with succession when both the offices of President and Vice-President are vacant.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Prime Minister
(b) Other Ministers
(c) Governors
(d) Judges of the Supreme Court

List-II
(i) Appointed by the President
(ii) Appointed by the President
(iii) Appointed by the President
(iv) Appointed by the President
mcqs.explanation: The President appoints the Prime Minister, other Ministers, Governors and Judges of the Supreme Court.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Judges of the High Courts
(b) Comptroller and Auditor General
(c) Attorney General
(d) Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
(e) Members of the Union Public Service Commission
(f) Election Commissioners
(g) Members of the Finance Commission

List-II
(i) Attorney General
(ii) Comptroller and Auditor General
(iii) Judges of the High Courts
(iv) Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
(v) Members of the Union Public Service Commission
(vi) Election Commissioners
(vii) Members of the Finance Commission
options: a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i, e-v, f-vii, g-vi
a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv, e-vii, f-vi, g-v
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-v, e-iv, f-vii, g-vi
a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv, e-v, f-vi, g-vii
mcqs.explanation: The President appoints Judges of the High Courts, the CAG, the Attorney General, the UPSC Chairman and members, Election Commissioners, and members of the Finance Commission. Therefore, option 1 gives all the correct pairs.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President normally appoints the leader of the majority party as Prime Minister.
Reason (R): The President can seek information from the Prime Minister under Article 78.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President normally appoints the leader of the majority party as Prime Minister, while Article 78 enables the President to seek information from the Prime Minister; the latter does not explain the former.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The President is an integral part of Parliament under Article 79.
II. The President summons and prorogues Parliament and dissolves the Lok Sabha.
III. The President addresses Parliament under Article 87.
IV. The President assents to Bills under Article 111.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The President is an integral part of Parliament, summons and prorogues it, dissolves the Lok Sabha, addresses Parliament under Article 87, and assents to Bills under Article 111.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the veto powers of the President:

I. The President has the power of absolute veto.
II. The President has the power of suspensive veto.
III. The President has the power of pocket veto.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The President has all three veto powers listed: absolute veto, suspensive veto and pocket veto.

mcqs.question: How many members does the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.explanation: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President appoints Judges of the Supreme Court.
Statement B: The President appoints Judges of the High Courts.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President appoints Judges of the Supreme Court as well as Judges of the High Courts.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are powers of the President under Article 72?

1. Granting reprieves
2. Granting respites
3. Granting remissions
4. Suspending sentences
mcqs.explanation: All four listed powers are included under Article 72: the President can grant reprieves, respites and remissions, and can suspend sentences.

mcqs.question: Article 63 of the Constitution provides for which of the following?
options: The office of the President of India
The office of the Vice-President of India
The term of office of the Vice-President
mcqs.explanation: Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India.

mcqs.question: Who constitutes the Electoral College for the election of the Vice-President of India?
options: Members of Parliament and members of State Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament only
Members of both Houses of Parliament, elected as well as nominated
Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament, including elected and nominated members. State Legislative Assemblies do not participate.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of the Vice-President is incorrect?
options: The resolution must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
The removal resolution is passed by the Rajya Sabha.
The resolution is passed by a simple majority of the Rajya Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the type of majority. The Rajya Sabha resolution requires a majority of all the then members of the Council, not a simple majority.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Reason (R): Article 64 provides for the Vice-President to hold this position.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 64 specifically provides that the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Article 63
(b) Article 64
(c) Article 66
(d) Article 67

List-II
(i) Office of the Vice-President
(ii) Term of office
(iii) Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
(iv) Election of the Vice-President
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Article 63—office of the Vice-President; Article 64—ex-officio Chairman; Article 66—election; Article 67—term of office.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the election of the Vice-President:

I. Members of both Houses of Parliament, elected as well as nominated, participate.
II. State Legislative Assemblies participate.
III. The election uses proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote.
IV. The election is conducted by secret ballot.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct. State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the Vice-Presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Vice-President addresses his resignation to the President.
Statement B: The oath of the Vice-President is administered by the President.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Vice-President resigns by addressing the President, and the oath is administered by the President.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are qualifications prescribed for election as Vice-President?

1. Citizen of India
2. Completed 35 years of age
3. Qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
4. Does not hold any office of profit
mcqs.explanation: Three listed conditions are correct: Indian citizenship, completion of 35 years, and not holding an office of profit. The Vice-President must be qualified for election as a Rajya Sabha member, not a Lok Sabha member.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum period for which the Vice-President may act as President when the office of President falls vacant or the President is unable to discharge functions?
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President may act as President for a maximum period of six months, within which the election for a new President must be held.

10.title: Chief Minister: Powers, Articles and Key Facts

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional position of the Chief Minister in a State?
options: The Chief Minister is the real executive head, while the Governor is the nominal or constitutional head
The Chief Minister is the nominal head, while the Governor is the real executive head
The Chief Minister and Governor are jointly the real executive heads
The Governor is the head of the Council of Ministers, while the Chief Minister is its nominal head
mcqs.explanation: The Chief Minister is the real executive head of the State and heads the State Council of Ministers. The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Chief Minister acts as a link between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers.
Reason (R): Article 167 requires the Chief Minister to communicate decisions of the Council of Ministers and proposals for legislation to the Governor.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The communication and information-related duties specified under Article 167 explain the Chief Minister’s linking role between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Governor is the head of the State, while the Chief Minister is the head of the Government
In the case of a hung Assembly, the Governor has discretionary power in appointing the Chief Minister
The Chief Minister advises the Governor on the appointment of other Ministers
The Chief Minister is responsible only to the Legislative Council
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is 'Legislative Council'. The Chief Minister is responsible only to the Legislative Assembly, not to the Legislative Council.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and is normally the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly.
Statement B: A person appointed Chief Minister need not be a member of the State Legislature at the time of appointment, but must become a member within six months.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, normally choosing the majority party leader, and a non-member must enter the State Legislature within six months.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the size of the State Council of Ministers:
I. The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
II. The minimum strength in smaller States is 12, including the Chief Minister.
III. The 15% limit is calculated on the total strength of the Legislative Council.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct under the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. Statement III is incorrect because the limit is based on the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First woman Chief Minister
(b) First non-Congress Chief Minister
(c) Chief Minister of Delhi/Puducherry
(d) Oath of the Chief Minister administered by

List-II
(i) President
(ii) Sucheta Kripalani
(iii) Governor
(iv) E.M.S. Namboodiripad
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: (a)-ii, Sucheta Kripalani; (b)-iv, E.M.S. Namboodiripad; (c)-i, President; and (d)-iii, Governor.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are associated with the Governor?
1. The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.
2. The oath of the Chief Minister is administered by the Governor.
3. The resignation of the Chief Minister is addressed to the Governor.
4. The Chief Minister of Delhi/Puducherry is appointed by the Governor.
mcqs.explanation: The first three statements are correct. The Chief Minister of Delhi/Puducherry is appointed by the President under Article 239AA, so statement 4 is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Reason (R): If a No-Confidence Motion is passed, the entire Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, must resign.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The requirement that the entire Council, including the Chief Minister, resign after losing a No-Confidence Motion reflects its collective responsibility to the Legislative Assembly under Article 164(2).

mcqs.question: Under which Article is the Governor appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal?
mcqs.explanation: Article 155 provides that the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the qualifications of the Governor is incorrect?
options: The person must have completed 35 years of age.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person should not hold any office of profit.
The person may continue as a member of Parliament after becoming Governor.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that a Governor may continue as a member of Parliament. A Governor should not be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature; if already a member, the person must vacate the seat.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The normal term of office of a Governor is five years, but the Governor may leave office earlier or continue longer.
Reason (R): The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Although the normal term is five years, the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President, permitting earlier removal or continuation beyond five years.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head of the State.
Statement B: The real executive authority is exercised by the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the constitutional position of the Governor described in the notes.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The emoluments and allowances of the Governor are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
II. If the same person is Governor of two or more States, the salary is shared in the proportion determined by the President.
III. The oath of the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The notes connect the Governor’s salary with the State Consolidated Fund, provide for Presidential determination of shared salary, and assign oath administration to the concerned High Court’s Chief Justice.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 153
(b) Article 154
(c) Article 159
(d) Article 213

List-II
(i) Oath of the Governor
(ii) Governor for each State
(iii) Executive power of the State vested in the Governor
(iv) Promulgation of Ordinances
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iii, c-i and d-iv.

mcqs.question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?
options: The Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
The Chief Minister of the State
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 159, the oath of the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Governor’s pardoning power is limited to offences against State laws.
Reason (R): Article 161 provides the Governor with the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, and to suspend or commute sentences.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason only describes the types of relief available under Article 161; it does not explain the specific limitation to offences against State laws.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of an independent State.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the State. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh, whereas Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal and the first woman Governor of an independent State.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are discretionary powers of the Governor?
1. Appointment of the Chief Minister in case of a hung Assembly
2. Dismissal of a Council of Ministers that has lost its majority
3. Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
4. Recommending President’s Rule under Article 356
mcqs.explanation: All four listed actions are included among the Governor’s discretionary powers.

mcqs.question:
Match the features in List-I with the corresponding provisions or descriptions in List-II:
List-I
(a) Appointment of the Governor
(b) Removal of the Governor
(c) Ordinance-making power of the Governor
(d) Pardoning power of the Governor

List-II
(i) Pleasure of the President
(ii) Article 213
(iii) Electoral College
(iv) Article 161
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-i, c-ii and d-iv: the Governor is appointed by the President, holds office during the President’s pleasure, promulgates Ordinances under Article 213, and exercises pardoning power under Article 161.

12.title: Lok Sabha Membership: Composition and Qualifications

mcqs.question: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha under Article 81?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552. This includes not more than 530 members from the States and not more than 20 members from the Union Territories.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding qualification for membership of the Lok Sabha is incorrect?
options: The person must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person must be registered as a voter in any State Legislative Assembly constituency.
The person must be at least 25 years of age.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the reference to a State Legislative Assembly constituency. The notes specify that the person must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years from the date of its first sitting.
Reason (R): The Lok Sabha can be dissolved earlier by the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. However, the President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha earlier does not explain its normal five-year term.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Anglo-Indian nomination to the Lok Sabha was abolished after 25 January 2020 by the 104th Constitutional Amendment.
Statement B: Reservation of Lok Sabha seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was last extended by the 104th Amendment till 2030.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes state that Anglo-Indian nomination was abolished after 25 January 2020 and that SC/ST reservation was extended till 2030 by the 104th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 81
(b) Article 83
(c) Article 84
(d) Article 330

List-II
(i) Qualification for membership
(ii) Reservation for SC/ST
(iii) Composition
(iv) Duration
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Article 81—Composition, Article 83—Duration, Article 84—Qualification, and Article 330—Reservation for SC/ST.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker.
II. A person who becomes a member of both Houses must choose one within 10 days.
III. A Minister who is not a member of either House must get elected within six months.
IV. The strength of the Council of Ministers is limited to 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are supported by the notes. They cover the Speaker's role under the Anti-Defection Law, the ten-day choice rule, the six-month election requirement for a non-member Minister, and the 15% limit.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are listed as conditions under which a Lok Sabha seat becomes vacant?
I. Resignation addressed to the Speaker
II. Disqualification
III. Absence for 60 days without permission
IV. Becoming a member of the other House
mcqs.explanation: All four are listed conditions for vacancy of a Lok Sabha seat. The notes specifically mention resignation to the Speaker, disqualification, unauthorised absence for 60 days, and becoming a member of the other House.

13.title: Rajya Sabha Composition and Special Powers

mcqs.question: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha according to Article 80?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250, comprising not more than 238 elected representatives and 12 nominated members.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding qualification for membership of the Rajya Sabha is incorrect?
options: The person must be not less than 25 years of age.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency.
The person must be not less than 30 years of age.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the minimum age of 25 years. For Rajya Sabha membership, the minimum age is 30 years.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List in the national interest.
Reason (R): Such authorisation requires a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha may authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 80
(b) Article 83(1)
(c) Article 84
(d) Fourth Schedule

List-II
(i) Qualification
(ii) Allocation of seats
(iii) Composition
(iv) Duration as a permanent House
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii: Articles 80, 83(1) and 84 deal with composition, duration and qualification respectively, while the Fourth Schedule deals with allocation of seats.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Rajya Sabha is elected indirectly by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
II. The election uses proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote.
III. The Rajya Sabha is subject to dissolution after every six-year term.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution, so statement III is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Only three Union Territories—Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir—have representation in the Rajya Sabha.
Statement B: The quorum of the Rajya Sabha is one-tenth of its total membership.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. The three represented Union Territories are Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir, and the quorum is one-tenth of total membership.

mcqs.question: To whom is the resignation of a Rajya Sabha member addressed?
options: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
