Match List-I with List-II on the basis of the immediate chronological predecessor of each case.

List-I
(a) Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain
(b) Maneka Gandhi
(c) Kihoto Hollohan
(d) S.R. Bommai

List-II
(i) Kesavananda Bharati
(ii) Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain
(iii) Minerva Mills
(iv) Kihoto Hollohan
mcqs.explanation: The chronology is Kesavananda Bharati → Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain → Maneka Gandhi → Minerva Mills → Kihoto Hollohan → S.R. Bommai. Hence each pairing in option 1 identifies the immediate predecessor correctly.

mcqs.question: Which case reinforced and approved the Basic Structure Doctrine?
options: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
mcqs.explanation: Minerva Mills v. Union of India reinforced and approved the Basic Structure Doctrine. It also struck down clauses giving absolute precedence to the DPSPs over Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.question: The 39th Constitutional Amendment was nullified by which Amendment?
mcqs.explanation: The 39th Amendment, linked to Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain, was nullified by the 44th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India expanded Article 21 by recognizing personal liberty, including the right to travel abroad.
Reason (R): The case held that the procedure affecting personal liberty must be just, fair, and reasonable.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India expanded Article 21 in relation to personal liberty and the right to travel abroad. It also held that the procedure affecting such liberty must be just, fair, and reasonable.

mcqs.question: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India was decided in which year?
mcqs.explanation: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India was decided in 1978.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala is incorrect?
options: The case held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights under any circumstances.
The case propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine.
The case was heard by a 13-Judge Bench.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights under any circumstances. Kesavananda Bharati held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot alter or destroy the Basic Structure; the key issue was the Basic Structure Doctrine.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II on the basis of the year of decision.

List-I
(a) Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
(b) Berubari Union Case
(c) Golaknath v. State of Punjab
(d) Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain

List-II
(i) 1967
(ii) 1951
(iii) 1975
(iv) 1960
mcqs.explanation: Shankari Prasad was decided in 1951, Berubari Union in 1960, Golaknath in 1967 and Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain in 1975.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras was decided in 1950.
Reason (R): The case concerned preventive detention and focused on the meaning of “procedure established by law” under Article 21.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The year of decision does not explain why the case concerned preventive detention or procedure established by law.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Champakam Dorairajan was decided in 1951.
Statement B: The decision led directly to the First Constitutional Amendment, 1951.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Champakam Dorairajan was decided in 1951, and it led directly to the First Constitutional Amendment, 1951, which inserted Article 15(4).

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh:

I. The key issue in Shankari Prasad was Parliament’s power to amend Fundamental Rights.
II. Article 368 was linked to Shankari Prasad.
III. Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan was decided in 1965.
IV. Sajjan Singh reaffirmed Parliament’s power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Shankari Prasad was linked to Parliament’s amendment power and Article 368, while Sajjan Singh in 1965 reaffirmed the power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala:

I. It was decided in 1973.
II. It propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine.
III. It recognized the Preamble as part of the Constitution.
mcqs.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati was decided in 1973, propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine and recognized the Preamble as part of the Constitution.

mcqs.question: Which case restored the balance between Part III and Part IV of the Constitution?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
mcqs.explanation: Minerva Mills v. Union of India restored the balance between Part III and Part IV by striking down clauses giving absolute precedence to the Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India was decided in 1978.
Statement B: The case established that Articles 14, 19 and 21 are mutually inclusive.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Maneka Gandhi was decided in 1978. It widened Article 21 and established the golden triangle in which Articles 14, 19 and 21 are mutually inclusive.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain was decided in 1975.
Statement B: The case was linked to the 39th Constitutional Amendment.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain was decided in 1975 and was linked to the 39th Constitutional Amendment, parts of which were struck down.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II on the basis of the constitutional provision or amendment linked to each case.

List-I
(a) Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillu
(b) S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
(c) P. Sambamurthy v. State of A.P.
(d) Minerva Mills v. Union of India

List-II
(i) 32nd Constitutional Amendment
(ii) 42nd Constitutional Amendment
(iii) 52nd Amendment and Tenth Schedule
(iv) Article 356
mcqs.explanation: Kihoto Hollohan was linked to the 52nd Amendment and Tenth Schedule; S.R. Bommai to Article 356; P. Sambamurthy to the 32nd Amendment; and Minerva Mills to clauses of the 42nd Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India expanded Article 21 in relation to personal liberty and travel abroad.
Statement B: The decision linked Articles 14, 19 and 21.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Maneka Gandhi expanded Article 21 by recognising personal liberty, including the right to travel abroad. It also established the interrelationship of Articles 14, 19 and 21.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements regarding Minerva Mills v. Union of India are correct?
1. It was decided in 1980.
2. It reinforced the Basic Structure Doctrine.
3. It concerned the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy.
4. It struck down unconditional precedence of Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Minerva Mills, decided in 1980, reinforced the Basic Structure Doctrine, restored the balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs, and struck down clauses giving DPSPs unconditional precedence.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: P. Sambamurthy v. State of A.P. was linked to the 32nd Constitutional Amendment.
Statement B: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillu was linked to the 52nd Amendment and the Tenth Schedule.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: P. Sambamurthy was associated with the 32nd Amendment. Kihoto Hollohan concerned the 52nd Amendment and the Tenth Schedule relating to the Anti-Defection Law.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Golaknath v. State of Punjab preceded Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala chronologically.
Reason (R): Golaknath completely prohibited Parliament from amending Fundamental Rights.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Golaknath was decided in 1967, before Kesavananda Bharati in 1973. Golaknath did completely prohibit amendment of Fundamental Rights, but that fact does not explain the chronological order.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Kesavananda Bharati allowed amendment of Fundamental Rights subject to the Basic Structure boundary.
2. Kesavananda Bharati propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine.
3. Minerva Mills reinforced the Basic Structure Doctrine.
4. Minerva Mills completely prohibited every amendment of Fundamental Rights.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Kesavananda Bharati permitted amendments subject to the Basic Structure limitation and propounded the doctrine, while Minerva Mills reinforced it; the fourth statement is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II on the basis of the constitutional issue or doctrine associated with each case.

List-I
(a) Berubari Union Case
(b) Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
(c) Minerva Mills v. Union of India
(d) S.R. Bommai v. Union of India

List-II
(i) Preamble is not part of the Constitution
(ii) Basic Structure Doctrine
(iii) Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution
(iv) Balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Berubari–Preamble not part, Kesavananda Bharati–Basic Structure Doctrine, Minerva Mills–balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs, and S.R. Bommai–Preamble integral.

25.title: Election Commission: Powers, Roles and Reforms

mcqs.question: The Election Commission of India derives its constitutional status primarily from which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The Election Commission of India is a permanent, independent constitutional body under Part XV, covering Articles 324–329.

mcqs.question: The Election Commission of India was established on:
mcqs.explanation: The ECI was established on 25 January 1950. This date has been celebrated annually as National Voters’ Day since 2011.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The ECI conducts elections to the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
The ECI conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
The ECI conducts elections to the offices of President and Vice-President.
The ECI conducts elections to State Assemblies and State Councils.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the ECI conducts Panchayat and Municipal elections. These elections fall under the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): All three members of the Election Commission have equal powers.
Reason (R): Decisions in the Election Commission are taken by majority.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. However, the fact that decisions are taken by majority does not explain why all three members have equal powers.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 324
(b) Article 243K
(c) Article 243ZA
(d) Article 326

List-II
(i) Universal Adult Suffrage
(ii) State Election Commission for Panchayat elections
(iii) Election Commission of India
(iv) State Election Commission for Municipal elections
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Article 324—ECI; Article 243K—Panchayat elections; Article 243ZA—Municipal elections; Article 326—Universal Adult Suffrage.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding removal safeguards?
options: Other Election Commissioners may be removed by the President on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Chief Election Commissioner may be removed directly by the Governor on the recommendation of the President.
Regional Commissioners may be removed by the President on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Chief Election Commissioner is removed in like manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge.
mcqs.explanation: The fourth statement is incorrect. The notes provide removal safeguards for the CEC and state that other ECs and Regional Commissioners are removed by the President on the CEC’s recommendation; they do not assign this power to the Governor.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The ECI advises the President on disqualification of Members of Parliament.
Statement B: The ECI advises the Governor on disqualification of Members of State Legislatures.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Under Article 103, the President decides MP disqualification based on the ECI’s binding opinion, while under Article 192, the Governor decides MLA/MLC disqualification based on that opinion.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 325 provides for a single general electoral roll.
II. Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
III. Article 326 provides for universal adult suffrage for Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly elections.
IV. The right to vote is a Fundamental Right according to the Kuldip Nayar Case.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. The Kuldip Nayar Case treated the right to vote as a legal/statutory right, not a Fundamental Right, so statement IV is incorrect.

mcqs.question: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years through the:
mcqs.explanation: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Amendment Act, 1988, effective from 1989.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Model Code of Conduct is not an Act of Parliament.
Reason (R): It is an ECI-formulated guideline enforced from the announcement of the election schedule.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason explains the assertion. The MCC is formulated and enforced by the ECI from the date the election schedule is announced, rather than being a parliamentary Act.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) EVM
(b) EPIC Voter ID
(c) VVPAT
(d) NOTA

List-II
(i) 1993
(ii) September 2013
(iii) 1982
(iv) September 2013
mcqs.explanation: The correct chronology-based pairs are EVM—1982, EPIC Voter ID—1993, VVPAT—September 2013, and NOTA—September 2013.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following election-related developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of EPIC Voter ID
B. Introduction of VVPAT
C. EVM used at Parur, Kerala
D. Introduction of NOTA
mcqs.explanation: The correct order is EVM at Parur in 1982, EPIC Voter ID in 1993, VVPAT in September 2013, and NOTA in September 2013.

mcqs.question: A candidate contesting an election to the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly can contest from a maximum of how many constituencies under Section 33 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
mcqs.explanation: Under Section 33 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate can contest from a maximum of two constituencies.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Election Commission of India is a permanent body.
Statement B: The Election Commission of India is an independent body.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Election Commission of India is both a permanent and an independent constitutional body.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Article 324(1) vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
Reason (R): Article 324 belongs to Part XV of the Constitution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 324(1) assigns superintendence, direction and control of elections to the ECI, while its placement in Part XV does not explain that assignment.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chief Election Commissioner in the ECI
(b) Election Commissioners in the ECI
(c) Appointment of the CEC and Election Commissioners
(d) Tenure of an Election Commissioner

List-II
(i) Six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
(ii) Two
(iii) The President of India
(iv) One
mcqs.explanation: The ECI consists of one CEC and two Election Commissioners. The President appoints them, and an Election Commissioner's tenure is six years or up to 65 years, whichever is earlier.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Election Commission of India is a multi-member body.
II. The ECI has been a multi-member body continuously since 1 October 1993.
III. The Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners receive salaries equivalent to those of Supreme Court Judges.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The ECI is a multi-member body, has continuously had this character since 1 October 1993, and its three members receive salaries equivalent to those of Supreme Court Judges.

mcqs.question: The removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner is provided under which provision of the Constitution?
mcqs.explanation: The removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner is provided under Article 324(5).

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 243K
(b) Article 243ZA
(c) Part IX
(d) Part IX-A

List-II
(i) Constitutional basis of the State Election Commission relating to Panchayats
(ii) Constitutional basis of the State Election Commission relating to Municipalities
(iii) Part containing Article 243K
(iv) Part containing Article 243ZA
mcqs.explanation: Articles 243K and 243ZA form the constitutional basis of the State Election Commission. Article 243K belongs to Part IX, while Article 243ZA belongs to Part IX-A.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India?

1. Lok Sabha elections
2. Rajya Sabha elections
3. State Legislative Assembly elections
4. State Legislative Council elections
5. Presidential elections
6. Vice-Presidential elections
7. Gram Panchayat elections
8. Panchayat Samiti elections
9. Zilla Parishad elections
mcqs.explanation: The ECI conducts the first six categories: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, State Legislative Councils, Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections. Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zilla Parishad elections are conducted by the State Election Commission.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Elections to Municipalities
(b) Elections to Municipal Corporations
(c) Removal of the head of the Election Commission of India
(d) Removal of the head of the State Election Commission

List-II
(i) Like a Supreme Court Judge
(ii) Like a High Court Judge
(iii) Conducted by the State Election Commission
(iv) Conducted by the State Election Commission
mcqs.explanation: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Municipalities and Municipal Corporations. The head of the ECI is removed like a Supreme Court Judge, while the head of the SEC is removed like a High Court Judge.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The State Election Commission operates under the respective State Panchayati legislation.
Statement B: The State Election Commission operates under the respective State Municipal legislation.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The State Election Commission operates under the respective State Panchayati legislation and State Municipal legislation.

mcqs.question: The right to vote in India is classified as:
mcqs.explanation: The right to vote is a legal right and a statutory right. It is not a Fundamental Right.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President decides the disqualification of Members of Parliament under Article 103.
Reason (R): The President's decision is based on the binding opinion of the Election Commission of India.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 103, the President decides disqualification of Members of Parliament. The decision is based on the binding opinion of the Election Commission of India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor decides the disqualification of Members of Legislative Assemblies and Members of Legislative Councils under Article 192.
Statement B: The Governor's decision is based on the binding opinion of the Election Commission of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 192, the Governor decides the disqualification of MLAs and MLCs. The Governor's decision is based on the binding opinion of the Election Commission of India.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Registration of political parties
(b) Allotment of election symbols
(c) Adjudication of political party merger disputes
(d) Adjudication of political party split disputes

List-II
(i) Representation of the People Act, 1951
(ii) Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968
(iii) Function of the Election Commission of India
(iv) Function of the Election Commission of India
mcqs.explanation: The ECI registers political parties under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. It allots symbols under the Election Symbols Order, 1968 and adjudicates political party merger and split disputes.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following conditions for recognition as a national party:

I. Winning at least 2% of Lok Sabha seats from at least three different States.
II. Securing at least 6% of valid votes polled in Lok Sabha or Assembly elections in at least four States and winning at least four Lok Sabha seats.
III. Being recognized as a State Party in at least four States.

Which of the above conditions are correct?
mcqs.explanation: A political party can qualify as a national party by satisfying any one of the three listed conditions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Election notifications for Parliament are issued by the President.
Statement B: Election notifications for State Legislatures are issued by the Governor.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Election notifications for Parliament are issued by the President, while notifications for State Legislatures are issued by the Governor.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Election Commission of India
(b) Election Commission of India
(c) President or Governor
(d) Delimitation Commission
(e) Delimitation Commission

List-II
(i) Election notifications
(ii) Recommendation of election dates
(iii) Determination of election schedule
(iv) Execution of constituency delimitation
(v) Constitution under parliamentary law
mcqs.explanation: The ECI recommends election dates and determines the election schedule, but it does not issue election notifications. Notifications are issued by the President or Governor, while constituency delimitation is executed by a Delimitation Commission established under parliamentary law.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned in court.
Reason (R): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be modified by legislatures.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes state separately that Delimitation Commission orders cannot be questioned in court and cannot be modified by legislatures; the second statement does not explain the first.

mcqs.question: A candidate forfeits the security deposit when the candidate fails to secure more than which proportion of the total valid votes polled?
mcqs.explanation: The security deposit is forfeited if a candidate fails to secure more than one-sixth of the total valid votes polled.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Location of introduction of VVPAT
(b) First Chief Election Commissioner
(c) Period of service of the first Chief Election Commissioner
(d) First woman Chief Election Commissioner
(e) Year in which V. S. Ramadevi served as Chief Election Commissioner

List-II
(i) Noksen, Nagaland
(ii) Sukumar Sen
(iii) 1950–1958
(iv) V. S. Ramadevi
(v) 1990
mcqs.explanation: VVPAT was introduced at Noksen in Nagaland. Sukumar Sen was the first CEC and served from 1950 to 1958; V. S. Ramadevi was the first woman CEC and served in 1990.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding simultaneous elections:

I. Amendment of Article 83 may be required.
II. Amendment of Article 85 may be required.
III. Amendment of Article 172 may be required.
IV. Amendment of Article 174 may be required.
V. Amendment of Article 356 may be required.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III, IV and V
II, III, IV and V only
mcqs.explanation: The notes identify Articles 83, 85, 172, 174 and 356 as provisions that may require amendment for simultaneous elections.

mcqs.question: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body established under which Article of the Constitution?
mcqs.explanation: The Finance Commission is established under Article 280 in Part XII of the Constitution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Finance Commission submits its report to the President.
The report is laid along with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.
The Finance Minister lays the Finance Commission report before Parliament.
The President causes the report to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the authority laying the report. The report is laid by the President, not the Finance Minister.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Finance Commission consists of five members, including one Chairman and four other members.
Reason (R): The qualifications of its members are determined by Parliament by law.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The composition of five members and the determination of qualifications by Parliament are separate provisions, so the Reason does not explain the Assertion.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. First Finance Commission
 b. 14th Finance Commission
 c. 15th Finance Commission
 d. State Finance Commission

List-II
 i. N.K. Singh
 ii. Governor of the State
 iii. K.C. Neogy
 iv. Y.V. Reddy
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: First Finance Commission—K.C. Neogy; 14th Finance Commission—Y.V. Reddy; 15th Finance Commission—N.K. Singh; State Finance Commission—Governor of the State.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Finance Commission recommends the distribution of net proceeds of divisible Union taxes between the Centre and the States.
II. It recommends the allocation of the States' share among the States.
III. It recommends principles governing grants-in-aid of State revenues out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
IV. It resolves legal disputes between the Centre and States under Article 131.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III describe Finance Commission functions. Statement IV is incorrect because disputes under Article 131 are resolved by the Supreme Court under its Original Jurisdiction.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 275 deals with statutory grants-in-aid to States.
Statement B: Article 282 deals with discretionary grants for any public purpose outside the legislative purview of the Union or a State.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 275 concerns statutory grants-in-aid, while Article 282 concerns discretionary grants for public purposes outside the relevant legislative purview.

mcqs.question: The Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India:
options: Only once during the President's term
Every five years or earlier as deemed necessary
Every ten years or earlier as decided by Parliament
mcqs.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted every five years or earlier if the President considers it necessary; the interval is not rigidly fixed at five years.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The 14th Finance Commission recommended an increase in States' share of net divisible taxes from 32% to 42%.
Reason (R): The Finance Commission is an anchor of fiscal federalism and recommends the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Finance Commission's role in recommending the distribution of net tax proceeds explains its relevance to the States' share of divisible taxes.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following Articles are specifically associated with the Finance Commission and its grants or report?

1. Article 275
2. Article 280
3. Article 281
4. Article 360
mcqs.explanation: Three Articles are specifically associated with the Finance Commission and its functions: Article 275 concerns grants-in-aid, Article 280 establishes the Finance Commission, and Article 281 concerns its report. Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)?
options: It is a Constitutional body established under the Constitution
It is a Statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
It is a Statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1992
It is an executive body established by the Union Cabinet
mcqs.explanation: The NHRC is a statutory, independent body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It is not a Constitutional body.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the NHRC's High-Level Selection Committee is incorrect?
options: The committee consists of six members, including the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Prime Minister is the Chairperson of the Selection Committee
The President of India appoints the NHRC based on the committee's recommendations
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the Selection Committee
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, not the Chairman, represents the Rajya Sabha on the Selection Committee.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The NHRC is a statutory body and not a Constitutional body.
Reason (R): It was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Establishment under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 explains why the NHRC has statutory rather than Constitutional status.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The NHRC is appointed by the President of India, whereas the SHRC is appointed by the Governor of the State.
Statement B: The NHRC deals with matters on the Union List, Concurrent List and at the national level, whereas the SHRC deals with matters under the State List and Concurrent List.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements correctly state the appointment authorities and the respective jurisdictional areas of the NHRC and SHRC.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the NHRC:
I. It has the powers of a Civil Court while inquiring into complaints.
II. It may visit jails and detention centres to study the living conditions of inmates.
III. Its recommendations are binding and it directly executes criminal sentencing.
IV. It has direct and unrestricted investigative powers over the armed forces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The NHRC's recommendations are advisory, and it does not have direct or unrestricted investigative powers over the armed forces.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) NHRC — Appointed by
(b) SHRC — Appointed by
(c) NHRC — Selection head
(d) SHRC — Selection head

List-II
(i) Governor of the State
(ii) Chief Minister
(iii) President of India
(iv) Prime Minister
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: NHRC—President of India, SHRC—Governor of the State, NHRC selection head—Prime Minister, and SHRC selection head—Chief Minister.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following correctly describe the institutional hierarchy or mechanisms under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
1. NHRC functions at the national level.
2. SHRC functions at the state level.
3. Human Rights Courts provide a district/trial mechanism for speedy trials.
4. NHRC functions at the state level.
mcqs.explanation: The first three statements are correct. The fourth is incorrect because NHRC is the national-level institution; SHRC functions at the state level.

mcqs.question: Under the statutory procedure concerning the armed forces, what does the NHRC do?
options: It calls for an independent report from the Central Government and makes recommendations based on that report
It transfers every complaint to the SHRC for investigation
It directly imposes criminal sentencing on members of the armed forces
It directly investigates all complaints without restriction
mcqs.explanation: The NHRC does not have direct or unrestricted investigative powers over the armed forces. It calls for an independent report from the Central Government and makes recommendations based on that report.

mcqs.question: The Punchhi Commission was primarily associated with which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The Punchhi Commission was the second major Commission on Centre–State Relations and Indian Federalism.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Rajamannar Committee was appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government to examine Centre–State Relations.
The Punchhi Commission was appointed to review working, conventions, judicial interpretations and dialogue mechanisms governing Centre–State Relations.
The Indrajit Gupta Committee was related to Centre–State Relations.
The Sarkaria Commission recommended the establishment of a permanent Inter-State Council.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement concerns the Indrajit Gupta Committee. It was related to State funding of elections, not Centre–State Relations.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Inter-State Council has a constitutional basis under Article 263.
Reason (R): It was formally set up on 28 May 1990 following the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 263 provides the constitutional basis, while the date and Sarkaria Commission recommendation describe its establishment; the Reason does not explain the constitutional basis.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Punchhi Commission
(b) Sarkaria Commission
(c) Rajamannar Committee
(d) Indrajit Gupta Committee

List-II
(i) State funding of elections
(ii) State-level initiative for federal autonomy
(iii) Federal dialogue and coordination mechanisms
(iv) Recommendation for a permanent Inter-State Council
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Punchhi Commission–Federal dialogue and coordination mechanisms; Sarkaria Commission–Recommendation for a permanent Inter-State Council; Rajamannar Committee–State-level initiative for federal autonomy; Indrajit Gupta Committee–State funding of elections.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Inter-State Council was established by the President of India.
Statement B: The Inter-State Council was established by an Act of Parliament.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: the Inter-State Council was established by the President of India. Statement B is false because it was not enacted or established by Parliament.

29.title: Lok Sabha Rules and Parliamentary Procedures

mcqs.question: Under which Lok Sabha Rule is the No-Confidence Motion governed?
mcqs.explanation: The No-Confidence Motion is governed by Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure. It is not mentioned in the Constitution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A No-Confidence Motion is introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
It requires written notice to the Secretary-General.
Support of at least 30 members is required for leave to be granted.
It is moved against the entire Council of Ministers.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the number of supporting members. At least 50 members must support the motion for leave to be granted.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Zero Hour is not a constitutional provision.
Reason (R): Zero Hour is an informal convention and is not mentioned in the Constitution or the Rules of Procedure.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Zero Hour is an informal parliamentary convention and is not provided in the Constitution or the Rules of Procedure.

mcqs.keyword: Questions in Parliamentary Proceedings (Starred, Unstarred, Short Notice)
mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A starred question requires an oral answer and permits supplementary questions.
Statement B: An unstarred question requires a written answer and permits supplementary questions.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true. Statement B is false because supplementary questions are not allowed for an unstarred question.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. Rule 198
 b. Rule 184
 c. Rule 377
 d. Rule 8(1)

List-II
 i. Election of the Deputy Speaker
 ii. No-Confidence Motion
 iii. Special Mention of Matters
 iv. Discussion followed by voting
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-iii and d-i. Rule 198 concerns the No-Confidence Motion, Rule 184 discussion with voting, Rule 377 special mentions, and Rule 8(1) the Deputy Speaker’s election procedure.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Question Hour is the first hour of every sitting.
II. Zero Hour immediately follows Question Hour.
III. Question Hour is an informal convention not mentioned in the Rules.
IV. Zero Hour is used to raise urgent matters of great public importance.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct. Question Hour is a formal procedure under the Rules, whereas Zero Hour is an informal convention.

mcqs.keyword: Questions in Parliamentary Proceedings (Starred, Unstarred, Short Notice)
mcqs.question:
How many of the following types of questions allow supplementary questions?
1. Starred Question
2. Unstarred Question
3. Short Notice Question
mcqs.explanation: Two types allow supplementary questions: Starred Questions and Short Notice Questions. Supplementary questions are not allowed for Unstarred Questions.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of matters that may be raised per day under Rule 377, as increased in 2015?
mcqs.explanation: The number of matters under Rule 377 was increased from 20 to 30 matters per day in 2015.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): An Adjournment Motion involves an element of censure or condemnation against the government.
Reason (R): It interrupts normal business to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance and recent occurrence.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the interruption of normal business and discussion of an urgent recent matter describes the motion’s procedure rather than explaining why it contains censure or condemnation.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Money Bills are connected with Article 110.
Statement B: Joint sittings are connected with Article 108.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes: Money Bills are associated with Article 110 and Joint Sittings with Article 108.

mcqs.question: The Chief Justice of India and the Supreme Court of India are dealt with under which constitutional Part, Chapter and Article range?
mcqs.explanation: The Head of the Union Judiciary and the Supreme Court of India are covered under Part V, Chapter IV, Articles 124–147.

mcqs.question: Under Article 124(2), who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
options: The senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
mcqs.explanation: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President under Article 124(2). By convention, the senior-most Supreme Court judge is appointed as CJI.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The CJI holds office until attaining the age of 65 years.
The oath of the CJI is administered by the President or a person appointed by the President.
The resignation of the CJI is addressed in writing to the President of India.
The CJI has a fixed tenure of five years.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the fixed five-year tenure. The CJI holds office until attaining 65 years; no fixed term in years is prescribed in the notes.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): An Acting Chief Justice is appointed when the office of the Chief Justice is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform duties.
Reason (R): The Acting Chief Justice is appointed by the President under Article 126.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 126 provides for appointment of an Acting CJI by the President when the CJI's office is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform duties.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 126
(b) Article 127
(c) Article 128
(d) Article 129

List-II
i. Supreme Court as a Court of Record
ii. Attendance of retired judges at Supreme Court sittings
iii. Appointment of an Acting Chief Justice
iv. Appointment of ad hoc judges
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 126–Acting Chief Justice, Article 127–ad hoc judges, Article 128–attendance of retired judges, and Article 129–Court of Record.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following developments in the correct chronological order:
A. Third Judges Case
B. First Judges Case
C. 99th Amendment and NJAC
D. Second Judges Case
mcqs.explanation: The sequence is First Judges Case (1981), Second Judges Case (1993), Third Judges Case (1998), and the 99th Amendment and NJAC (2014–15).

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 131 deals with the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction over federal disputes.
II. Article 136 confers discretionary appellate power through Special Leave Petition.
III. Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its own pronouncements.
IV. Article 143 deals with the Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct according to the constitutional articles listed in the notes.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Advice tendered by the Supreme Court under Article 143 is binding on the President in all cases.
Statement B: On pre-Constitution disputes, the Supreme Court is bound to give advice.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is false because advice tendered under Article 143 is not binding on the President. Statement B is true for pre-Constitution disputes.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding removal of a Supreme Court judge is incorrect?
options: The grounds are proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Removal is made by an order of the President.
The procedure is governed by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
The removal address requires a simple majority in each House of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the majority requirement. Removal requires a special majority in each House: a majority of the total membership plus at least two-thirds of members present and voting in the same session.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 130
(b) Article 131
(c) Article 136
(d) Article 137

List-II
i. Review of judgments or orders
ii. Seat of the Supreme Court
iii. Original jurisdiction
aiv. Special Leave Petition
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Article 130–seat of the Supreme Court, Article 131–original jurisdiction, Article 136–Special Leave Petition, and Article 137–review.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Under Article 129, the Supreme Court is a Court of Record.
2. The Court of Record includes the power to punish for contempt of itself.
3. Under Article 130, the seat of the Supreme Court is Delhi.
4. The CJI may decide another place with the President's approval.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Article 129 concerns the Court of Record and contempt power, while Article 130 provides for Delhi as the seat, with another place possible through the specified approval.

mcqs.question: Under which Article of the Constitution is the office of the Attorney General of India provided?
mcqs.explanation: The Attorney General of India is a constitutional post under Article 76.

mcqs.question: Who appoints the Attorney General of India?
options: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
mcqs.explanation: The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President of India.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Attorney General of India is incorrect?
options: The Attorney General may be removed at any time by the President.
The remuneration of the Attorney General is fixed by Parliament.
The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.
The remuneration of the Attorney General is determined by the President.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that remuneration is fixed by Parliament. According to the notes, it is determined by the President.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Attorney General of India has no fixed constitutional tenure.
Reason (R): The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Since the Attorney General holds office during the President's pleasure, the Constitution does not prescribe a fixed tenure.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Attorney General of India has the right of audience in all courts within the territory of India while performing official duties.
Reason (R): The right of audience is available to the Attorney General while performing official duties.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason directly states the condition attached to the Attorney General's right of audience.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Attorney General of India is a constitutional post under Article 76.
Statement B: The Solicitor General of India is a non-constitutional or statutory post.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Attorney General is a constitutional post under Article 76, whereas the Solicitor General is a non-constitutional or statutory post created to assist the Attorney General.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
I. The Attorney General can speak in either House of Parliament.
II. The Attorney General can vote on any motion or bill.
III. The Attorney General can be named a member of and participate in any Parliamentary Committee.
IV. The Attorney General is entitled to the privileges and immunities of a Member of Parliament under Article 105(4).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct. The Attorney General may speak and participate in committees but cannot vote on any motion or bill.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Attorney General of India — Constitutional basis
(b) Advocate General of the State — Constitutional basis
(c) Solicitor General of India — Constitutional status
(d) Attorney General of India — Appointing authority

List-II
(i) Article 165
(ii) President of India
(iii) Non-Constitutional / Statutory
(iv) Article 76
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Attorney General—Article 76; Advocate General—Article 165; Solicitor General—Non-Constitutional/Statutory; Attorney General's appointing authority—President of India.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are correctly associated with the Attorney General of India?
1. Article 76 — Office, appointment, duties and pleasure
2. Article 88 — Rights with respect to the Houses of Parliament
3. Article 105(4) — Powers, privileges and immunities
4. Article 165 — Office of the Attorney General of India
mcqs.explanation: The first three associations are correct. Article 165 concerns the Advocate General for the State, not the Attorney General of India.

32.title: Advocate General and State Legislature Privileges

mcqs.question: Who appoints the Advocate General of a State?
options: The Chief Minister of the State
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 165(1), the Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor of the State.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Advocate General of a State is incorrect?
options: The Advocate General has a fixed constitutional tenure under Article 165(3).
The Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters.
The Advocate General is the highest law officer and official legal adviser to the State Government.
The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is “fixed constitutional tenure.” Under Article 165(3), the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor and has no fixed constitutional tenure.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Advocate General of a State must be qualified to be appointed as a Judge of a High Court.
Reason (R): The qualification of a High Court Judge is referred to under Article 217.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Advocate General must possess the qualification for appointment as a High Court Judge, as referred to in Article 217.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Advocate General of the State
(b) Attorney General of India
(c) Solicitor General of India

List-II
(i) Article 76, Part V
(ii) Assists the Attorney General
(iii) Article 165, Part VI
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Advocate General of the State—Article 165, Part VI; Attorney General of India—Article 76, Part V; Solicitor General of India—assists the Attorney General.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General under Article 177:

I. The Advocate General can speak in the proceedings of both Houses of the State Legislature.
II. The Advocate General can participate in joint sittings of the State Legislature.
III. The Advocate General can be named a member of and participate in any State Legislative Committee.
IV. The Advocate General can vote on any motion or bill in the State Legislature.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct rights under Article 177. The Advocate General is not a member of the State Legislature and cannot vote on a motion or bill.
